newsitem.title: USA: Ex-Stifel banker Cochran to report to jail Monday.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Stifel banker Cochran to report to jail Monday.

text.p: Former Stifel, Nicolaus & Co investment banker Robert Cochran is scheduled to report Monday to an Oklahoma prison to begin serving a seven-year sentence for rigging tax-exempt bond bids in return for undisclosed fees, according to lawyers.
Cochran is to report to El Reno Correctional Institution in El Reno, Oklahoma on noon Monday, according to attorneys in the case.

A federal jury convicted the ex-Stifel vice president May 6 of eight out of 21 counts of cheating the Oklahoma City Airport Trust Authority and the Sisters of St. Mary Health Care Authority on bond deals authorized by the panels.
U.S. District Judge Ralph Thompson sentenced Cochran in late August to seven years and three months in prison plus a three-year suspended sentence following the prison term.
Thompson also ordered Cochran to return $629,000 in illegal profits on a $76.7 million airport trust bond issue and a $265 million healthcare authority deal.
He also ordered Cochran to pay part of a $489,000 restitution charge and to pay a $50,000 fine.
Cochran associate Michael Garrett was acquitted by jurors on three wire fraud charges involving the bond deals.
Last August, Stifel's St. Louis-based parent company agreed to pay a record $1.4 million fine to settle related securities charges brought by the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Stifel neither admitted or denied the charges.
